title: PipeThreader: Software-Defined Pipelining for Efficient DNN Execution
problem: DNN execution on distributed systems requires efficient pipelining and parallelism strategies; fixed hardware pipelines limit flexibility and performance optimization.
motivation: Software-defined pipelining enables dynamic optimization of DNN execution patterns based on model architecture and hardware capabilities.
method: PipeThreader replaces fixed hardware pipelines with software control over how deep neural networks (DNNs—large models built from many computational layers) are divided into processing stages. The key mechanism is dynamic adjustment: as the neural network runs, the software can change both how many pipeline stages exist and how work is distributed across processors based on what the computation needs. This orchestration (coordination) enables the system to optimize for whatever hardware and workload it encounters. Instead of being locked into one design, the parallelism strategy—how many independent data paths run in parallel—adjusts on the fly.
key_novelty: PipeThreader's core idea is using software to dynamically define and adjust neural network pipelines instead of relying on fixed hardware designs.
limitations: Software overhead may limit effectiveness for latency-critical workloads.
